test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sum of money amounts to 3 times the original sum in 15 years. In how many years will the original sum amount to 5 times of itself at the same rate of simple interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Time = 15 years 

**Formula used:**

S.I. = (P × R × T )/100 

S.I. = Simple Interest, P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, T = Time in years 

**Calculation:**

 Here, Let the original sum be P then,

According to the Question given,

Amount after 15 years = 3P 

⇒ S.I. =( A - P) = ( 3P - P) = 2P , Time = 15 years

⇒ S.I. = ( P × R × T )/ 100 

⇒ 2P =( P × R × 15) /100 

⇒ 2× 20 /3 = R 

⇒ R = 40/3%

Now, in 2nd condition given in the Question, Amount becomes 5P and Rate of interest remains same 

⇒ S.I. = ( A - P ) = ( 5P - P) = 4P , R = 40/3

⇒ S.I. = ( P × R × T) / 100 

⇒ 4P = ( P × 40 × T) / 3×100 

⇒ T = 30 years

**Hence, the required years is 30.**
